claims.claim: Xiaomi's general privacy policy says a user can request a free copy of personal information Xiaomi processes.
claims.evidence: Section 9 states that a copy of personal information processed by Xiaomi will be provided upon request free of charge, subject to stated limits.

claims.claim: Where applicable law provides it, Xiaomi recognizes a right to receive personal information in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
claims.evidence: The policy's Right to data portability names a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and transmission to another controller.

claims.claim: Xiaomi can require enough information to verify the identity and authority of a person making a privacy request.
claims.evidence: The linked support portal is Xiaomi's request channel; the policy says requests must provide sufficient information to verify identity and authority.

claims.claim: The current Mi Fitness iOS listing supports Xiaomi Watch, Redmi Watch, Xiaomi Smart Band and Redmi Smart Band families.
claims.evidence: The Xiaomi-controlled listing names all four product families.

claims.claim: Mi Fitness displays route-tracked workouts, heart rate, sleep, stress, energy, manual weight and women's-health data, sleep stages and personalized sleep reports on supported products.
claims.evidence: The current listing describes workout routes; heart rate, sleep, stress and energy; manual weight and women's health; deep/light/REM stages; breathing quality and personalized reports.

claims.claim: Xiaomi Smart Band 10 displays SpO2, VO2 max, Training Load and Recovery Time and provides on-wrist running courses.
claims.evidence: The product page names all-day SpO2, VO2 max, training load, recovery time and ten built-in on-wrist running courses.

claims.claim: Xiaomi Smart Band 10 provides Sleep Score, a 21-day sleep-improvement plan and Vitality Score.
claims.evidence: The product page names Sleep Score and Vitality Score and says the band offers a 21-day plan based on prior sleep data.

claims.claim: Xiaomi Watch S4 provides on-wrist running courses and Running Form Recognition for vertical ratio, vertical amplitude and ground contact time.
claims.evidence: The product page explicitly names on-wrist running courses, Running Form Recognition and the three posture metrics.

claims.claim: The current Android Mi Fitness listing says the app synchronizes fitness and health data to Google Health Connect.
claims.evidence: The listing's Health Connect permission purpose is: Synchronize your fitness and health data to Google Health Connect.

claims.claim: Health Connect stores typed activity, body, sleep, vitals and other health/fitness records with instant, interval or series structures.
claims.evidence: Google's data-type catalogue defines categories and record types and documents per-type permissions.

claims.claim: A user-authorized Android application can read Health Connect records and can request additional background-read permission.
claims.evidence: Google documents ReadRecordsRequest and the READ_HEALTH_DATA_IN_BACKGROUND permission.

claims.claim: Gadgetbridge can operate supported wearables locally without the vendor application or a vendor account.
claims.evidence: The canonical project describes using Bluetooth gadgets without the vendor's closed-source app and without creating an account or transmitting data to vendor servers.

claims.claim: Gadgetbridge is a direct device-management route and does not establish retrieval of prior Mi Fitness cloud history.
claims.evidence: The project describes pairing and managing gadgets locally instead of relying on the proprietary app; it does not claim to be a Xiaomi account-history client.

claims.claim: Gadgetbridge Xiaomi support is model specific; several current devices are experimental, and Smart Band 7 Pro can synchronize only the current day's activities.
claims.evidence: The Xiaomi catalogue marks multiple current devices experimental and warns that Smart Band 7 Pro cannot synchronize an earlier day's unsynced activity.

claims.claim: Android's health-samples repository is reference code for Health Connect applications rather than a complete Xiaomi exporter.
claims.evidence: The repository describes individual Android Studio projects that help developers get started writing Android and Wear OS health applications.
